hook: Every photograph starts in the dark. *So did we.*
dek: How a camera bag, a question and a father's byline became The Innovators Den.

slides.text: Wally showed up with *camera bags* and a plan: film Dominican artists in New York and stream it live back home to the DR.

slides.label: The question
slides.text: I loved the passion. I didn't see the profit. That model was *underexposed*. So I asked him: *What about a podcast?*

slides.label: Ink in the blood
slides.text: My father, Anselmo Silverio, was a *journalist* in the Dominican Republic. When I said podcast, part of me was saying *Dad*.

slides.label: The inheritance
slides.text: Some sons inherit a watch. *I inherited the press*: the pressure of his name, the push to press forward, and the calling itself.

slides.label: Making our mark
slides.text: The name came first: *The Innovators Den*. Our first shoot was at *Wally's mom's house*. Every den starts as somebody's home.

slides.label: My first beat
slides.text: With Jade, about four, and Daniel, barely one, my first stories were *spoken*, not written: on dog walks and drives to drop-off.

slides.label: The pride
slides.text: *Naliyah, Jade and Daniel.* Without them, there is no me. Without my father, no story. Without that season, *no Den*.

slides.label: Lost without a beat
slides.text: Then the mics went quiet, and I was lost. No story to chase, no rhythm, no heartbeat. *So we came back.*

cta_line: We are The Innovators Den. *Welcome home.*
question: What's the story that got YOU started?

Every photograph starts in the dark. So did we.

In 2022, Wally showed up with camera bags and a plan. I asked him one question: "What about a podcast?" What I didn't say out loud was that I was trying to reach my father, a journalist in the DR, through the only language we both spoke. The story.

From Wally's mom's house to dog walks and school drop-offs, this is how The Innovators Den was born, and why we came back.
